chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from Abu al-Jawza', from al-Husayn ibn 'Alwan, 'Amr ibn Khalid, from Zayd ibn 'Ali, from his fathers, from 'Ali (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him) forbade the meat of domestic donkeys and the marriage of Mut'ah. The approach in this narration is to attribute it to taqiyya (dissimulation), because it agrees with the schools of the general public (Sunni). The earlier narrations agree with the apparent meaning of the Book and the consensus of the True Sect upon its requirement, so it is obligatory to act upon them rather than this unusual narration.
ai.seo_question: Why is the prohibition of Mut'ah marriage in some narrations considered to be due to taqiyya?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Istibsar, the scholar analyzes the prohibition of Mut'ah marriage by attributing it to taqiyya, a strategic dissimulation employed to align with the prevailing Sunni consensus. He contrasts this with the stronger evidence derived from the Quran and the consensus of the 'true sect' (Ithna Ashari), concluding that the prohibition is an exceptional report to be set aside in favor of permissibility.
